statement: By using the generalised binomial theorem, show that the coefficient of $x^{r}$ in $(1-x)^{-n}$ (with $n$ a positive integer) is $\\binom{n+r-1}{r}$. Hence find the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in $(1-2x)^{-4}$.
solution:
$(1-x)^{-n}=\\sum_{r=0}^{\\infty}\\dfrac{(-n)(-n-1)\\cdots(-n-r+1)}{r!}(-x)^{r}=\\sum_{r=0}^{\\infty}\\dfrac{n(n+1)\\cdots(n+r-1)}{r!}x^{r}=\\sum_{r=0}^{\\infty}\\binom{n+r-1}{r}x^{r}$. For $(1-2x)^{-4}$ we take $n=4$ and replace $x$ by $2x$, so the coefficient of $x^{3}$ is $\\binom{4+3-1}{3}(2)^{3}=\\binom{6}{3}\\cdot8=20\\cdot8=160$.
